guidance.procedure: Inspect the complete operative definition, not isolated nouns. For technical-only coverage, determine whether the protected class is exclusively technical; express inclusion of commercial, financial, business, oral, visual, or other material opposes that limitation. For explicit identification, require a universal marking or designation condition; broad confidentiality language alone is neutral, while coverage expressly independent of labeling opposes such a requirement. For oral information, include any designation and later written-confirmation conditions. Cite every fragment that completes the definition or condition, but exclude headings and illustrative material that adds no rule.

Analyze disposition, retention, and survival separately. For return or destruction, identify the exact trigger: termination language can support the termination proposition, whereas a demand or request alone does not. Preserve whether the duty covers all information or only specified forms and whether return and destruction are alternatives. For post-disposition possession, an express backup, archive, legal-retention, or dispute exception supports retention; a requirement to return or destroy all information and copies without an exception supports the opposed boundary. For survival, require obligations expressly continuing beyond termination, not merely a fixed agreement term. Cite operative rules and responsive exceptions, not adjacent headings or enforcement clauses.

Decide each proposition independently by matching actor, action, recipient class, quantifier, and condition. Employee disclosure answers the employee proposition; consultants, agents, advisers, contractors, affiliates, or other non-employees may answer the third-party proposition only when the clause actually authorizes disclosure to that class. Preserve the observed distinction between an affirmative need-to-know authorization and a prohibition relieved only by discretionary written consent; do not turn the latter into a general permission. For copying, a necessity- or purpose-limited exception to a no-copy rule supports some permissible copying, while an unqualified no-copy duty supports opposition. Cite the operative authorization or prohibition and any fragment needed to state its condition, excluding recipient-notice duties and generic secrecy language.

Trace each exception as a grammatical chain from any operative exclusion lead-in to the responsive subparagraph. Independent development requires development without use of, reference to, or access to protected information. Third-party acquisition requires an external source entitled to disclose and, when stated, free of a confidentiality duty; public-domain and prior-possession exceptions are not substitutes. Compelled disclosure permission and a notice duty are separate: verify legal compulsion, whether notice is required or excused, protective-order opportunity, and any required-portion limit. Cite the lead-in when it supplies the exclusion or scope and every responsive continuation, but not a standalone heading or neighboring exception.

Resolve actor, modality, action, object, scope, and exceptions before choosing a relation. Reverse engineering requires direct reverse-engineer, decompile, test, or equivalent language concerning protected material; confidentiality, copying, ownership, or ordinary use restrictions are not substitutes. Solicitation requires recruiting, soliciting, inducing departure, hiring, or comparable conduct directed at the specified people, including all fragments carrying the actor and exceptions. No-license requires express no-grant, no-license, or no-right language; ownership alone is insufficient. Agreement confidentiality requires protection of its existence, terms, or negotiations. Limited use requires an operative restriction to the stated purpose, together with any operative purpose definition that delimits it, not generic secrecy language or a heading.

Evaluate breadth, identification, and communication form as separate propositions after reading the complete operative definition. Technical-only coverage requires the protected class to remain exclusively technical; inclusion of business, financial, commercial, or other non-technical material opposes it. Explicit identification requires a universal marking or designation condition, while coverage regardless of labeling opposes it. For oral or visual information, preserve any contemporaneous designation and later written-confirmation requirements. Cite every fragment needed to complete the applicable definition or condition, but exclude headings, illustrative categories that add no rule, and unrelated neighboring clauses.

This update adds an observed technical-only member contrast, retains a broad non-technical contrast and marking/oral examples, removes the less useful identification witness, and removes a same-source heading contrast.

Third, require obligations expressly continuing beyond termination for survival, rather than treating a fixed agreement term as survival.
